**Continuous 2.38.2**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.38.1, 2.38.0, 2.36.0, 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.38.2.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.38.2.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.38.2.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.38.2.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.38.2.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.38.2.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.38.2.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.38.2-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.38.2.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.38.2-vscode/continuous-cli-2.38.2.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.38.1

A request whose output cap is above the model's published maximum, or above the room left in the context window, is lowered before it is sent. A tool result that still fits the window is sent with that smaller cap, instead of ending the turn. The diagnostic log records why a turn stopped.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent.

### Fixes

- **Output cap.** Claude 4.5 asked for 128,000 output tokens is sent 64,000, which is that model's cap. A cap that already fits is left as it is. A thinking-budget raise cannot pass the fitted cap.
- **Large tool result.** On a 100,000-token window, a result of about 90,000 tokens no longer refuses the next request. The reply reserve shrinks from 10% of the window down to 1,000 tokens, and the output cap sent with the request shrinks to the room that is left. A result that cannot sit beside that 1,000-token reply is still refused.
- **Why a turn stopped.** The diagnostic log under the chat input names the API stop reason, how much of the turn was an answer, reasoning, or tool calls, the model, the cap that was sent and the configured cap when those differ, the context window, and whether the prompt was pruned. Copy puts the lines on the clipboard. A stop to compact, a steer, or a reply cut off before its tool calls is named in that log and, when the next request is not sent, in the chat.
